title: My 100-Day Plan
framing: This 100-day plan for stepping into a Developer Experience / Engineering Enablement leadership role is organized around three pillars: developer experience and internal platform ownership, engineering enablement and insights (DORA/SEI), and people leadership.

focus_areas.label: Baseline
focus_areas.description: Understanding the current state before proposing changes to it.

focus_areas.label: People
focus_areas.description: Building the relationships that everything else depends on.

focus_areas.label: Process
focus_areas.description: How platform, enablement, and metrics work actually gets governed and prioritized.

focus_areas.label: Technology
focus_areas.description: The platform, tooling, and AI-assisted engineering capability itself.

focus_areas.label: Personal
focus_areas.description: How I'm calibrating my own effectiveness in the role.

pre_start: Review whatever org chart, team roster, and existing platform/enablement documentation is available ahead of day one.
Identify the people worth shadowing early: whoever currently owns platform tooling, metrics reporting, and any existing enablement program.
Draft a lightweight assessment framework (what I want to know by day 30) so early conversations are structured, not just exploratory.
days_0_30: Inventory existing internal-platform capabilities: service catalog, golden paths/templates, self-service tooling, and how discoverable they actually are to engineers.
Audit current DORA/SEI metric collection: what's measured, how, data quality, and whether anyone acts on it today.
Run a skills/capacity pass on the team (a strength-grid style exercise) to understand current bench strength and gaps.
Map current developer toolchain adoption (source control, CI/CD, artifact management, security scanning) against what's actually approved and standard.
days_31_60: Synthesize the first-30-days findings into a current-state gap analysis and validate it with the team and key stakeholders.
Separate findings into quick wins vs. longer structural investments, and start sizing the latter.
days_61_100: Publish a baseline engineering-health scorecard as the explicit 'before' reference point for tracking improvement from here forward.

pre_start: Map the key stakeholder groups I'll need relationships with: engineering leadership, security, architecture, product, and platform partner teams.
Identify my own manager's expectations and how they'll define success for this role in the first 90-100 days.
days_0_30: 1:1 with every direct report and every key cross-functional partner before doing much else.
Sit in on any existing Community of Practice, guild, or enablement forum as a participant before touching it as an owner.
Listen more than I act — keep a running log of open questions and ideas rather than reacting to the first thing that looks broken.
days_31_60: Establish a regular 1:1 and team-meeting cadence, and set individual goals/development plans with each report.
Formalize a recurring stakeholder sync with security, architecture, and product so platform/enablement priorities stay aligned, not siloed.
Start actively coaching on career growth rather than just gathering context.
days_61_100: Deliver a first real round of performance and growth feedback to the team.
Take visible ownership of (or relaunch, if it's stalled) a Community of Practice forum for knowledge sharing and feedback collection.
Confirm cross-functional partnership agreements are working in practice, not just on paper — adjust cadence/scope as needed.

pre_start: Review existing engineering standards, governance docs, and whatever lifecycle process currently keeps platform content current.
Review the existing enablement program structure (workshops, coaching, learning paths) if one already exists.
days_0_30: Shadow the current platform-adoption process end to end, as an engineer would experience it, not just as documentation.
Understand how DORA/SEI metrics currently flow into action (or don't) — is there a real feedback loop from data to team-level improvement objectives?
Assess the governance and lifecycle process for platform content: how does anyone know if a golden path or doc is stale?
days_31_60: Propose lightweight governance improvements — e.g. explicit freshness/ownership expectations for golden paths and templates.
Pilot a cadence that ties DORA/SEI insights directly to team-level improvement objectives, in partnership with one or two engineering leaders.
Define an initial intake and prioritization process for the platform roadmap/backlog, rather than working from an ad hoc list.
days_61_100: Formalize the platform roadmap and backlog intake process as a repeatable, documented cadence.
Launch the first structured enablement workshop or coaching cohort under the new cadence.
Establish a recurring engineering-health review with leadership, using the baseline scorecard as the starting reference.

pre_start: Review the current toolchain end to end: source control, CI/CD, artifact management, security scanning, and any existing internal-platform tooling footprint.
Note where AI-assisted engineering practices are already being piloted informally, so I'm not proposing something that already exists.
days_0_30: Complete a hands-on audit of service-catalog completeness, scorecard coverage, and where self-service actually breaks down for engineers.
Identify the highest-friction gap in the current golden-path/template set — the thing engineers most often work around rather than use.
days_31_60: Pilot one concrete improvement with a volunteer team — a new golden-path template, an added scorecard dimension, or an AI-assisted engineering practice.
Evaluate DevSecOps gating coverage (dependency scanning, code scanning, secrets detection) against what's actually enforced in CI today.
days_61_100: Ship the first platform improvement to general availability and publish it in the service catalog.
Publish an updated golden-path/template catalog reflecting what changed.
Document initial AI-assisted engineering guidance for broader rollout, based on what the pilot actually showed.

pre_start: Get explicit clarity from my own manager on what success looks like at 30/60/100 days, in their words, not just my assumptions.
Identify my own learning gaps going in (specific platform tooling, industry/regulatory context) and set a lightweight plan to close them.
days_0_30: Deliberately favor listening and learning over doing — resist the urge to fix the first thing that looks broken.
Keep a personal log of open questions and quick-win ideas rather than acting on all of them immediately.
days_31_60: Check in explicitly with my own manager on progress against the expectations set before day one, and adjust course if the read differs from theirs.
Adjust my own working rhythm (meeting load vs. deep-work time) based on what the first month actually revealed about where my time is needed.
days_61_100: Do a formal self-review against the original 30/60/100 success measures, honestly noting what didn't go to plan.
Set explicit next-90-day goals with my manager, informed by the baseline scorecard and the team/stakeholder feedback gathered so far.
